onThisPage.to: Understanding Skin Health & Skin CancerWhat a skin check coversPatient guides

section.heading: What a skin check covers
paragraphs: A skin check is a clinical assessment of your skin and areas of concern. Your practitioner usually discusses your history, examines relevant areas, explains findings and plans next steps such as monitoring, a procedure or referral when appropriate.
This is a simplified educational overview. It does not replace individual assessment.

section.heading: Women's health across life stages
paragraphs: Women's healthcare needs can change across life stages. Discussions may cover reproductive health, screening, pregnancy-related care, menopause and midlife health, and ongoing preventive care.
What is discussed depends on individual needs and circumstances.

guideLink.label: Read the women's health patient guides

figure.alt: Diagram titled Women's Health Across Life Stages, showing five stages from contraception and reproductive health through screening discussions, pregnancy and postnatal care, menopause and midlife health, and ongoing preventive care.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of women's health across life stages.

onThisPage.to: About this topicUnderstanding menopause carePatient guides

section.heading: Understanding menopause care
paragraphs: A menopause discussion can help you recognise life-stage changes, talk about symptoms and concerns, review overall health and plan follow-up support.
Care is tailored to the individual. This overview does not describe a specific treatment plan.

figure.alt: Diagram titled Understanding Menopause Care, showing four steps: recognise life-stage changes, discuss symptoms and concerns, review overall health, and plan follow-up and support.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of menopause care discussions.

onThisPage.to: About this topicHow antenatal care is organisedPatient guides

section.heading: How antenatal care is organised
paragraphs: Antenatal care is usually organised around you and your GP. It may include early pregnancy booking, regular reviews, tests or referrals when needed, and postnatal follow-up.
Shared maternity care may also involve hospital teams when arranged.

figure.alt: Diagram titled How Antenatal Care Is Organised, with a central you-and-your-GP hub connected to early pregnancy booking, regular antenatal reviews, tests and referrals when needed, and postnatal follow-up.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of how antenatal care is organised.

onThisPage.to: Understanding Children's HealthPreparing for a child's GP visitPatient questions

section.heading: Preparing for a child's GP visit
paragraphs: It can help to bring health and vaccination records, note symptoms or development questions, discuss concerns with the GP, and agree next steps and follow-up.
Longer appointments can help when several issues need time.

guideLink.label: Read the children's health patient guides

figure.alt: Diagram titled Preparing for a Child's GP Visit, showing four steps: bring health and vaccination records, note symptoms or development questions, discuss concerns with the GP, and agree next steps and follow-up.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of preparing for a child's GP visit.

onThisPage.to: Understanding VaccinationsVaccination across life stagesPatient guides

section.heading: Vaccination across life stages
paragraphs: Vaccination needs can change across childhood, adolescence, adulthood and older age. Travel recommendations may also be relevant for some people.
Recommendations depend on age, history and individual circumstances.

figure.alt: Diagram titled Vaccination Across Life Stages, showing childhood, adolescence, adulthood, older age and travel when relevant.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of vaccination across life stages.

onThisPage.to: Understanding Preventive HealthcareThe preventive healthcare cyclePatient guides

section.heading: The preventive healthcare cycle
paragraphs: Preventive care is often a repeating cycle: review history and risks, discuss screening and prevention, arrange checks or vaccinations when appropriate, then follow up and plan again.
What is recommended varies for each person.

guideLink.label: Read the preventive healthcare patient guides

figure.alt: Diagram titled The Preventive Healthcare Cycle, showing four repeating steps: review history and risks, discuss screening and prevention, arrange checks or vaccinations when appropriate, and follow up and plan again.
figure.caption: Educational diagram of the preventive healthcare cycle.

section.heading: Healthy ageing care over time
paragraphs: Healthy ageing care can bring together preventive reviews, falls and mobility discussion, vaccination review, medicines review and regular GP follow-up.
Priorities change with individual health needs.

guideLink.label: Read the healthy ageing patient guides

onThisPage.to: Understanding Telehealth & Access To CareWhen a telehealth consultation may fitPatient guides

section.heading: When a telehealth consultation may fit
paragraphs: Telehealth may suit some concerns when a phone or video consultation is clinically appropriate. It helps to have a private space, a clear connection, and your medicines and questions ready.
In-person care is needed when examination, testing or treatment cannot be provided safely by telehealth. Telehealth is not for emergencies.

figure.caption: Educational diagram of when a telehealth consultation may fit.
